newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida strike had no effect on output - company.
newsitem.headline: Escondida strike had no effect on output - company.

text.p: The 18-day strike at Escondida copper mine had no effect at all on production or shipment levels, due to efforts by non-striking employees, Minera Escondida Ltda said.

"During the 15-day strike, production levels of ore, copper concentrate, copper cathode and product shipments were at normal levels. The result was possible due to the efforts of the remaining 85 percent of the Escondida employees who continued to work," it said in a statement.
Escondida confirmed an earlier announcement from the union that the strike was over and that workers were returning to their jobs in accordance with shift schedules.
Seventeen percent of Escondida's workforce of about 2,000 joined the strike, the statement said.
The mine, the world's largest copper pit, is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp plc.
